segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Hello, Sandy. How have you been getting on with your dissertation?

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: Fine, and I've been working hard on the various action points we agreed on our last tutorial.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Do you want to talk me through what you've done?

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: Yeah, sure. Well, we agreed on three main targets for me to aim for. The first one was to find out about suitable data analysis software.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Yes.

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: And what I decided to do was to look through catalogues specialising in IT.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: That's a good idea. What did you come up with?

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: I found the names of two promising ones.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Right. ·

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: But I also thought it'd be worthwhile talking to a lecturer.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Oh right. Who did you see?

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: Jane Prince. Do you know her? She's in the Computer Centre.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Yes, of course, she's the new Head.

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: Yes. Well, she was very helpful.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Oh, that's good. Did she suggest anything in particular?

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: Yeah. She recommended software called Vivat and said I should book up for a couple of practice sessions using Vivat.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Great. I'm sure you'll find them useful.

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: And, of course, the second target was to draw up a survey checklist which I ...

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Yes, you emailed me it last week.

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: Have you had a chance to look ... ?

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Of course, urn I think it's good. Very much on the right lines. I'd say your first two sections are spot on. I wouldn't suggest that you change anything there, but in section three you really do need to have questions on teaching experience.

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: Yeah. I was thinking that section looked a bit short.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Right.

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: And my third target was, do further reading on discipline.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Oh yes. I mentioned a couple of writers, didn't I?

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: Yes, well I got hold of the Banerjee and I thought that was excellent. But I'm afraid I didn't manage to get hold of the essays about classroom management - you know, the ones by Simon Ericsson. The bookshop said it was out of print and the library doesn't have a copy.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Oh right, and I'm afraid I've lent my copy to another student. What I suggest you do is try the library again - this time apply for it through the service called special loans. Have you done that before? You're entitled to six books a year.

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: Yes. No problem. That's what I'll do.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: So, lots of useful work done.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: So, let's look at some new targets. We'll start by having a chat about your Chapter One. I very much enjoyed reading it. Your written style is very clear and you've included lots of interesting descriptions of education in your target are() I've just got a couple of suggestions for some additional work.

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: Of course. Could I just ask- what do you think I should call it?

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Well, I'd go for something like Context Review. What do you think?

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: Well, short and to the point.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Exactly. Now, as regards specific areas to work on, I'd be quite interested to have a few more statistics about the schools in the different zones.

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: Oh, that wouldn't be a problem. I can get them from the Internet.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Great, and although you did make a reference to quite a few different writers, I think you should aim to cite more works written later than ~.

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: OK. That's more difficult, but I can try. When do you want that done by?

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Oh, it's not urgent. Urn I should aim for the end of term. But in the meantime, I think you should also be thinking about Chapter Two.

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: Should I be drafting it already?

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: No, but I think you should note down its main sections.

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: Yes. You know, I always find that the hardest part.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: I always find it helpful to put some ideas on index cards.

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: Yeah.

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: Urn . .. and then you can sort them, and even lay them out on the floor. It's a real help.

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: Well, I'll certainly try it! When would the deadline be for that?

segments.speaker: TUTOR
segments.en: My advice would be to get it done before you embark upon the research. You can always change it later if you need to.

segments.speaker: SANDY
segments.en: OK. I'll get going on that then.
